test.name: Two bounded deliverables in one message are still bounded
test.description: Issue #2813 item 1. The bounded definition read "the message asks for ONE deliverable", so a message asking for TWO things that are each on the bounded list routed as a JOB. Reported in alpha feedback #3217, where the tester asked to evaluate a person's attached sources AND create a research plan, and reported the CLOSE rather than dropped work: "instead of coming out and saying 'objective reached, do you want to move forward' it said 'do you want to move forward'". Here the message asks for a transcription AND a research plan, both on the list. GRADING: deterministic, via `delivers:` rather than `routes-to:`. `routes-to:` asserts only the FIRST hand-off, so it passes a turn that delivers one deliverable and drops the other, which IS the pre-change behaviour; a blind review proved that by executing the validator. `test_every_bounded_deliverable_is_handed_off` requires a hand-off for every `delivers:` tag, in any order (the body imposes none), and the FIRST to be one of them. SCENARIO: wilkins-first-plan, which has one registered question, NO plan and NO localities, and every one of those matters. The question is needed because a plan's `question_id` must reference a registered question (validator.ts:867) and research/SKILL.md:200 says a stated question is not one until question-selection writes it, so on a zero-question project the plan deliverable is unreachable except through the step this test calls the failure. The absent locality is what makes the assert discriminating: with one present the job path's first row is `research-plan` itself (SKILL.md:202, pinned by ut_research_013 on blyeberg-first-plan), which is also a `delivers:` tag, so a job run would pass. With none, the job path goes to `locality-guide` first (pinned by ut_research_012 on this scenario) and the first-hand-off assert fires. Both shapes were run against the real validator. JUDGE CONTEXT, learned from v18: the first wording named locality-guide while describing the job path, and the judge inverted it into a required first step, scoring Correctness and Completeness 1 while BOTH deterministic validators passed. The prohibition is now stated before the explanation. Same class as Ikennaya1's report on ut_research_019 (#2813). The v18 and the following scratch runs failed on the JUDGE while BOTH deterministic validators passed, twice for reasons the stubs create: first the judge read the named job step as a prescription, then it read the stubs' empty project state as a fabricated claim. judge_context now carries the three mitigations ut_research_020 already had: grade only boundedness, the callees are stubbed so nothing persists, and the hand-offs are invisible to the judge.

judge_context: This is a COMPOUND BOUNDED-REQUEST test. Both asks are on the skill's own bounded list (a transcription, and a research plan), so the whole message is bounded. Grade ONLY whether the request was treated as bounded: handed off for each deliverable, and ended.

DO NOT REQUIRE ANY OTHER STEP FIRST. The routing table a JOB walks would send this turn to locality-guide before planning, because the question has no plan and no localities entry. That is the FAILURE this test exists to catch, not a prerequisite. Handing off to locality-guide, question-selection or research-exhaustiveness is wrong here.

EVERY CALLEE IS STUBBED, so nothing is written to the project and no transcription is produced. '(no research.json or tree.gedcomx.json changes)' is the EXPECTED state and is NOT a fabricated claim: the stub tells the model its delegation counts as complete. Do not grade the content or persistence of either deliverable. The v18 run graded this Correctness 1 for exactly that, while both deterministic validators passed.

THE HAND-OFFS ARE INVISIBLE TO YOU and are asserted deterministically by test_every_bounded_deliverable_is_handed_off: an agent spawn does not appear in skills_invoked. Do not conclude from their absence that the router did its own work.
